en.headline: Lee Tung Avenue lantern display ends today after more than six weeks
en.dek: More than 800 traditional red and custom palace lanterns have hung over the 200-metre pedestrian street in Wan Chai since early September.
body: Lee Tung Avenue in Wan Chai is on the final day of its Moon Fest Lumiere lantern display, which has featured more than 800 traditional red lanterns and new palace lanterns along the 200-metre tree-lined walkway since early September.

The palace lanterns, introduced for the first time this year, incorporate paper-cutting style designs that depict Mid-Autumn legends including Hou Yi shooting the suns, Chang’e ascending to the moon, the Jade Rabbit preparing the elixir, and Wu Gang chopping the osmanthus tree, along with scenes of families making lanterns and sharing meals.

The avenue is open from 10am to 11pm, with the lanterns switched on from 5pm. Admission is free. The organisers said the display is subject to weather conditions and advised visitors to check the avenue’s announcements for the latest arrangements on this final day.

zh.headline: 灣仔利東街中秋燈籠展今日最後一天 逾800盞紅燈籠及宮燈懸掛
zh.dek: 利東街200米林蔭大道自九月初起懸掛逾800盞傳統紅燈籠及全新宮廷燈籠，今日為展示最後一日。
body: 灣仔利東街「彩燈·迎月」中秋燈籠展今日進入最後一天，自九月初起在200米長的林蔭大道上懸掛逾800盞傳統紅燈籠及今年首次推出的宮廷燈籠。
宮廷燈籠採用剪紙風格設計，描繪后羿射日、嫦娥奔月、玉兔搗藥、吳剛伐桂等中秋傳說，以及家庭製作燈籠和團圓飯等場景。
大道每日上午10時至晚上11時開放，下午5時起亮燈，入場免費。主辦方表示展示受天氣影響，市民可留意利東街公布的最新安排。
